{"id": "000009a8-0000-4000-8000-0000000009a8", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_0xegbYOTRw8UhQv63DUHxs", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: serverless-operation-review\\\\ndescription: Operational review for AWS serverless workloads (Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB, and event sources SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis) against the Well-Architected Serverless Applications Lens. Use when the user asks to review, audit, assess or health-check serverless functions or applications, or raises Lambda timeouts, throttling, concurrency, cold starts, memory sizing, missing dead-letter queues, events failing silently or dropped, poison-pill records, growing IteratorAge, duplicate SQS processing, deprecated runtimes, unauthenticated function URLs, or serverless cost and log-retention waste. Triggers \\'serverless review\\', \\'how healthy is my serverless workload\\', \\'audit the Lambda functions against best practices\\', \\'review my Lambda functions\\', \\'API Gateway review\\', \\'Step Functions review\\', \\'serverless ORR\\'. Load this skill before choosing subagent skills, and list it in preloaded_skills of every collection subagent.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  author: ankitsri-aws\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Reviews AWS serverless workloads \\\\u2014 Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB and Lambda event sources \\\\u2014 against the Well-Architected Serverless Applications Lens.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Serverless Operational Review\\\\n\\\\nConduct a structured operational review of an AWS serverless workload aligned with the\\\\n[AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/welcome.html)\\\\nand the\\\\n[Serverless Applications Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/welcome.html),\\\\nthe [Lambda best practices guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html),\\\\nand the\\\\n[CloudWatch recommended alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Best_Practice_Recommended_Alarms_AWS_Services.html)\\\\nreference.\\\\n\\\\nThis skill uses **AWS Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, EventBridge,\\\\nEventBridge Scheduler, Kinesis, CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, IAM, and Cost Explorer read-only APIs\\\\nonly**. It never mutates a resource.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nActivate this skill when the user asks to:\\\\n\\\\n- Review, audit, or assess serverless functions, APIs, state machines, or tables\\\\n- Check serverless best-practice compliance or run a serverless operational readiness review (ORR)\\\\n- Evaluate serverless reliability, performance, security, cost, or observability posture\\\\n- Diagnose recurring Lambda timeouts, throttles, OOM kills, cold starts, or silent event loss\\\\n- Understand why SQS messages are processed twice, why a stream is falling behind, or where\\\\n  asynchronous invocations are disappearing\\\\n- Find serverless cost waste (over-provisioned memory, x86 on Graviton-eligible runtimes, unbounded\\\\n  log retention, idle provisioned concurrency)\\\\n\\\\nDo **not** use this skill for container or database engine reviews. Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Amazon\\\\nRDS/Aurora, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon MSK have their own dedicated review skills.\\\\n\\\\n## Review Scope Model\\\\n\\\\nFive resource families, any subset of which is a valid scope:\\\\n\\\\n| Family | Resources | Reviewed standalone? |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Compute | Lambda functions, versions, aliases, function URLs | Yes |\\\\n| Event sources | SQS, SNS, EventBridge, EventBridge Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis | Only as attached to a function |\\\\n| API | API Gateway REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs and their stages | Yes |\\\\n| Orchestration | Step Functions state machines | Yes |\\\\n| Data | DynamoDB tables and global secondary indexes | Yes |\\\\n\\\\n## Guardrails\\\\n\\\\nThese rules are non-negotiable and apply to every step.\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read-only.** Never call a mutating API. Recommend remediation; never apply it. If the user asks\\\\n   you to fix a finding, state the exact command or IaC change and let them run it.\\\\n2. **Never disclose secret material.** When reporting on environment variables, report the **key\\\\n   name only** \\\\u2014 never the value, and never a partial value. The same applies to anything found in\\\\n   logs that looks like a credential, token, connection string, or private key.\\\\n3. **Bound the work.** Follow the budget agreed in Step 1. Never sweep every region without being\\\\n   asked.\\\\n4. **Disclose what you skipped.** Every report states which regions were skipped, which resources\\\\n   were truncated by the budget, and which checks could not run for lack of permission.\\\\n5. **Never invent a threshold.** Every severity comes from the check catalogs in `references/`, each\\\\n   citing its AWS source. If a check has no documented threshold, report it as `INFO` and say the\\\\n   threshold is workload-specific. Name the source wherever you state a number, chat replies included.\\\\n6. **One reply carries the review.** The only text you may send starts with the heading\\\\n   `# Serverless health review: <region>` (shape in `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md`).\\\\n   Any other text, including \\\\\"still waiting\\\\\" on a subagent wake-up, is not sent. Outage: \\\\\"nothing checked\\\\\".\\\\n7. **A finding is a table row with a check id.** Columns: check id, severity, observed value, source\\\\n   API, doc or threshold source. An observation without a check id is context, not a finding.\\\\n8. **Keep three states apart.** Measured zero, no datapoints, and never queried are different results.\\\\n9. **Never print a 12-digit AWS account ID.** Use the alias or the last four digits.\\\\n\\\\nDelegating? Follow `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` (prompt contents, wake-up rule).\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Review Checklist\\\\n\\\\nWork through these in order and track progress as you go. Each step depends on the output of the one\\\\nbefore it, and the detailed section for each carries the same step number.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Establish scope and budget, and state both in the opening lines of the final reply\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Discover the serverless inventory, skipping empty Regions\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Collect configuration detail for the families in scope\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Collect 7-day CloudWatch metrics and compute the derived values\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Collect and analyse logs, including the REPORT-line extraction\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: Assess alarm coverage against the Serverless Lens metric list\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: Analyse security posture and execution-role breadth\\\\n- [ ] Step 8: Analyse cost and quantify the savings opportunities\\\\n- [ ] Step 9: Evaluate everything collected against the check catalogs and assign severities\\\\n- [ ] Step 10: Generate the report, then run the pre-presentation checks\\\\n\\\\nSteps 4 through 8 are independent of each other once Step 3 is done, so collect them in whatever order\\\\nis convenient \\\\u2014 but do not start Step 9 until they have all either completed or been recorded as\\\\nskipped.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Establish Scope and Budget\\\\n\\\\nAsk the user what to review. Accept any of:\\\\n\\\\n- Specific resource names or ARNs plus their Region (for example \\\\\"review the `checkout-processor`\\\\n  function in `eu-west-1`\\\\\")\\\\n- An application or stack boundary (a CloudFormation/SAM stack name, or a tag such as\\\\n  `Application=checkout`)\\\\n- All resources of a family in named Regions (\\\\\"all Lambda functions in us-east-1 and us-west-2\\\\\")\\\\n- All resources in all configured account Regions\\\\n\\\\nIf the user gives no scope, default to **all resource families in the caller\\'s current Region** and\\\\nsay so explicitly in the opening lines of the final reply.\\\\n\\\\n### Budget guardrail\\\\n\\\\nA wide serverless account can hold thousands of functions. Before collecting, state the plan and the\\\\ncap:\\\\n\\\\nDefault caps and the selection rule for each scope (named resources, stack or tag boundary,\\\\nnamed Regions, all Regions) are in `references/budget-and-cost-tables.md`. Read it before collecting.\\\\n\\\\nPut the budget in one line at the top of the final reply (not as a separate earlier message), for example:\\\\n\\\\n> Reviewing up to 25 Lambda functions, 10 API Gateway APIs, 10 state machines and 25 DynamoDB tables\\\\n> in `us-east-1`, selected by 7-day invocation volume. I will list anything I skip.\\\\n\\\\nIf the user asks for a bigger sweep, raise the cap \\\\u2014 but warn that a full multi-Region review of a\\\\nlarge account can take several hundred API calls and is best split by Region.\\\\n\\\\n**State the scope in the report.** Scope Covered lists the Regions, families, selection rule and caps\\\\napplied, even when the review finds nothing; \\\\\"no resources found\\\\\" means little without them.\\\\n\\\\n**Skip empty Regions.** Call the cheap list API first (`lambda:ListFunctions`,\\\\n`apigateway:GetRestApis`, `apigatewayv2:GetApis`, `states:ListStateMachines`,\\\\n`dynamodb:ListTables`); if a Region returns nothing for every family, record it as empty and move on\\\\nwithout further calls.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Discover Serverless Inventory\\\\n\\\\nPer in-scope Region, enumerate the families in scope:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nlambda.ListFunctions                 # paginated; FunctionVersion=ALL only if versions are in scope\\\\nlambda.GetAccountSettings            # account concurrency quota + code storage (once per Region)\\\\napigateway.GetRestApis               # REST APIs\\\\napigatewayv2.GetApis                 # HTTP + WebSocket APIs\\\\nstates.ListStateMachines             # state machines\\\\ndynamodb.ListTables                  # tables\\\\nlambda.ListEventSourceMappings       # paginated; maps functions to SQS/streams/MSK/Kafka\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nWrite the counts in your working notes before any deep collection, then pick the mode. Collect\\\\ninline unless a count exceeds 40 functions or 25 of another family; see\\\\n`references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` section 1. Do not call `subagent` before this line exists:\\\\n\\\\n`inventory: functions=N tables=N apis=N machines=N mappings=N -> mode: inline | delegate(<why>)`\\\\n\\\\nThe inventory table goes in the final reply, in this shape:\\\\n\\\\n| Type | Name | Region | Runtime / Protocol / Type | Key attribute |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Lambda | `checkout-processor` | us-east-1 | python3.13, arm64 | 1024 MB / 30 s |\\\\n| API (HTTP) | `checkout-api` | us-east-1 | HTTP | 2 stages |\\\\n| State machine | `order-saga` | us-east-1 | STANDARD | logging OFF |\\\\n| Table | `orders` | us-east-1 | PAY_PER_REQUEST | PITR off |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Collect Configuration Detail\\\\n\\\\nCollect per resource, for the families in scope. `references/collection-reference.md` lists the exact\\\\nAPI calls and the fields each one contributes to a check \\\\u2014 use it rather than improvising a call list,\\\\nbecause a field you skip is a check that silently cannot fire.\\\\n\\\\n| Family | Primary calls |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Lambda | `GetFunctionConfiguration`, `GetFunctionConcurrency`, `GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig`, `ListProvisionedConcurrencyConfigs`, `ListAliases`, `ListFunctionUrlConfigs`, `GetPolicy`, `ListTags` |\\\\n| Event sources | `sqs.GetQueueAttributes` (with `AttributeNames=All`), `sns.GetSubscriptionAttributes`, `events.ListTargetsByRule`, `scheduler.GetSchedule`, `kinesis.DescribeStreamSummary`, plus the event source mapping fields |\\\\n| API Gateway | `apigateway.GetStages`/`GetMethod`/`GetAuthorizers`/`GetUsagePlans`, `apigatewayv2.GetStages`/`GetRoutes`, `wafv2.GetWebACLForResource` |\\\\n| Step Functions | `states.DescribeStateMachine` (parse the ASL definition), `states.ListExecutions` |\\\\n| DynamoDB | `dynamodb.DescribeTable`, `DescribeContinuousBackups`, `DescribeTimeToLive`, `application-autoscaling.DescribeScalableTargets` |\\\\n\\\\nThe single most important cross-check in this step: **an SQS queue\\'s `VisibilityTimeout` against the\\\\nconsuming function\\'s `Timeout`**. A queue timeout below the function timeout produces duplicate\\\\nprocessing and is a CRITICAL finding \\\\u2014 see `references/checks-event-sources.md`.\\\\n\\\\nReport environment variables by **key name only**. Never the value.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Collect CloudWatch Metrics (7-Day)\\\\n\\\\nMake **one** `cloudwatch.GetMetricData` call per resource. `Period: 21600` (6 hours).\\\\n`StartTime`: 7 days ago. `EndTime`: now. Percentiles require `ExtendedStatistic`, not `Statistic`.\\\\n\\\\n`references/metrics-and-logs.md` lists the exact metric set per resource type \\\\u2014 Lambda (per function\\\\nand account level), SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, Kinesis, API Gateway, Step Functions, and\\\\nDynamoDB \\\\u2014 as `| id | metricName | stat | unit |` tables. Use it rather than improvising a metric\\\\nlist, so reports stay comparable between runs.\\\\n\\\\nA metric that returns no data because the configuration does not emit it is not a finding. Omit the\\\\nrow.\\\\n\\\\n### Derived values\\\\n\\\\nCompute these once and reuse them in Steps 6, 9, and 10:\\\\n\\\\n| Derived value | Formula | Used by |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Error rate | `Errors / Invocations` over the window | reliability findings |\\\\n| Throttle rate | `Throttles / (Invocations + Throttles)` | scaling findings |\\\\n| Timeout headroom | `Duration p99 / (Timeout \\\\u00d7 1000)` | performance findings |\\\\n| Concurrency headroom | `ClaimedAccountConcurrency / AccountLimit.ConcurrentExecutions` | scaling findings |\\\\n| Memory utilization | `Max Memory Used / MemorySize` (from Step 5) | cost and performance findings |\\\\n| PC utilization | `ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization` with `...SpilloverInvocations` | cost findings |\\\\n| Invocation cost weight | `Invocations \\\\u00d7 Duration(avg) \\\\u00d7 MemorySize` | cost split in Step 8 |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 5: Collect and Analyze Logs\\\\n\\\\nPer function, resolve the log group (`LoggingConfig.LogGroup`, default `/aws/lambda/<name>`) then:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nlogs.DescribeLogGroups   # logGroupNamePrefix; capture retentionInDays and storedBytes\\\\nlogs.FilterLogEvents     # 7-day window, one call per pattern, limit results\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nA log group that does not exist means the function has never been invoked \\\\u2014 report `INFO`, not a\\\\nfailure.\\\\n\\\\nTwo things to extract:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Error patterns** \\\\u2014 `references/metrics-and-logs.md` carries the pattern table (timeouts, OOM\\\\n   kills, import failures, ENI exhaustion, downstream throttling, permission denials, recursive-loop\\\\n   detection, socket timeouts). Record occurrence counts plus first and last occurrence for anything\\\\n   above zero.\\\\n2. **Memory and cold starts** \\\\u2014 every invocation emits a `REPORT` line carrying `Max Memory Used`,\\\\n   `Memory Size`, `Init Duration`, and `Billed Duration`. Parse **both** the text and JSON log\\\\n   formats; `LogFormat: JSON` moves these into `record.metrics`. Sample 200\\\\u2013500 REPORT lines across\\\\n   the window rather than scanning exhaustively, and state the sample size in the report.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 6: Assess Alarm Coverage\\\\n\\\\nFor each in-scope resource, call `cloudwatch.DescribeAlarmsForMetric` for the metrics the Serverless\\\\nApplications Lens names for that service. A missing alarm is a `MEDIUM` finding, and every reported\\\\ngap must carry the recommended statistic, threshold, period, and datapoints-to-alarm so the gap list\\\\ndoubles as an implementation plan.\\\\n\\\\nThe authoritative per-service list, with the recommended alarm settings, is in\\\\n`references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md`. Per-service metric lists are in that file.\\\\n\\\\nAlso assess the wider observability posture: `TracingConfig.Mode` on functions, `tracingEnabled` on\\\\nAPI stages and state machines, `LogFormat` (text logging is a `LOW` finding \\\\u2014 the Lens asks for\\\\nstructured JSON logging), and whether alarms exist at both the individual resource level and an\\\\naggregate level.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 7: Security and IAM Analysis\\\\n\\\\n### 7.1 Runtime currency\\\\n\\\\nCompare each function\\'s `Runtime` against `references/lambda-runtime-deprecations.md`. Never guess a\\\\ndeprecation date \\\\u2014 if the runtime is absent from the table, say the date is unverified and link the\\\\n[runtime support policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtimes.html).\\\\n\\\\n### 7.2 Execution role breadth\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\niam.GetRole\\\\niam.ListAttachedRolePolicies      # then iam.GetPolicy + iam.GetPolicyVersion per ARN\\\\niam.ListRolePolicies              # then iam.GetRolePolicy per inline policy\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFlag: `AdministratorAccess` or any `\\\\\"Action\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` with `\\\\\"Resource\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` (CRITICAL), service-level\\\\nwildcards such as `s3:*` or `dynamodb:*` (HIGH), `iam:PassRole` with `Resource: \\\\\"*\\\\\"` (HIGH), and a\\\\ntrust policy that allows a principal other than `lambda.amazonaws.com` without a condition (HIGH).\\\\n\\\\n**Summarise the policy; do not reproduce it.** Report the policy name and the specific offending\\\\nactions and resources as a short list \\\\u2014 for example \\\\\"inline policy `far-too-broad` grants\\\\n`dynamodb:*`, `sqs:*`, `sns:*` on `Resource: \\\\\"*\\\\\"`\\\\\". Do not paste the full policy JSON into the\\\\nreport. Beyond keeping the finding readable, verbatim policy documents have been observed to trip\\\\nthe agent\\'s content safety filter, which aborts the response mid-review and loses the whole report.\\\\n\\\\n### 7.3 Invocation exposure\\\\n\\\\n- `lambda.GetPolicy` \\\\u2014 a statement with `\\\\\"Principal\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` or `\\\\\"Principal\\\\\": {\\\\\"AWS\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"}` and no\\\\n  `SourceArn`/`SourceAccount` condition is CRITICAL\\\\n- `lambda.GetFunctionUrlConfig` \\\\u2014 `AuthType: NONE` is a public, unauthenticated HTTPS entry point.\\\\n  CRITICAL unless the user confirms it is intentionally public, in which case HIGH with a note to\\\\n  front it with CloudFront and WAF\\\\n- API Gateway stages with no authorizer and no API key and no WAF association \\\\u2014 HIGH\\\\n- `disableExecuteApiEndpoint: false` on an API that is only meant to be reached through a custom\\\\n  domain \\\\u2014 MEDIUM\\\\n\\\\n### 7.4 Data protection\\\\n\\\\n- Environment variables with no `KMSKeyArn` (Lambda-managed key only) \\\\u2014 MEDIUM when a key name\\\\n  suggests secret material. **Report key names only.** Recommend AWS Secrets Manager or SSM\\\\n  Parameter Store rather than environment variables for secrets\\\\n- Key-name heuristics that warrant the finding: `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN`, `API_KEY`,\\\\n  `APIKEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `CREDENTIAL`, `CONNECTION_STRING`, `DSN`, `AUTH`\\\\n- SQS queues and SNS topics without `KmsMasterKeyId` \\\\u2014 MEDIUM\\\\n- DynamoDB tables without a customer-managed key, where the workload handles regulated data \\\\u2014 LOW\\\\n  (AWS-owned key encryption is on by default)\\\\n- Functions with no `CodeSigningConfigArn` \\\\u2014 LOW\\\\n\\\\nIf a log-pattern scan surfaces what looks like a credential in a log line, report **that it happened\\\\nand in which log group**, never the value, and raise it as HIGH.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 8: Cost Analysis\\\\n\\\\nOnce per review, not per resource:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\ncostexplorer.GetCostAndUsage    # 3 months, MONTHLY, GroupBy USAGE_TYPE,\\\\n                                #   Filter Service IN [\\\\\"AWS Lambda\\\\\", \\\\\"AmazonCloudWatch\\\\\",\\\\n                                #   \\\\\"Amazon API Gateway\\\\\", \\\\\"Amazon DynamoDB\\\\\", \\\\\"AWS Step Functions\\\\\"]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nCost Explorer does not break Lambda spend down per function. Estimate a per-function share and label\\\\nit clearly:\\\\n\\\\n1. Take the most recent full month\\'s Lambda spend.\\\\n2. Weight each function by `Invocations \\\\u00d7 Duration(avg) \\\\u00d7 MemorySize` from Step 4.\\\\n3. Split the month total across functions by weight.\\\\n4. Mark every derived figure **(estimated)** in the report.\\\\n\\\\nQuantify these opportunities, each with its own finding. The signal and typical saving for each are in\\\\n`references/budget-and-cost-tables.md`. They are: memory rightsizing, Graviton migration, log retention, log volume, idle provisioned concurrency,\\\\nunused functions, DynamoDB capacity mode, and Step Functions type.\\\\n\\\\nAlways state that memory changes should be validated with\\\\n[AWS Lambda Power Tuning](https://github.com/alexcasalboni/aws-lambda-power-tuning) rather than\\\\napplied blind, because reducing memory also reduces CPU.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 9: Evaluate Against Best Practices\\\\n\\\\nEvaluate every collected value against the check catalogs, and assign exactly one severity per\\\\nfinding:\\\\n\\\\n| Catalog | Covers |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| `references/checks-lambda.md` | function configuration, concurrency, performance, security, cost |\\\\n| `references/checks-event-sources.md` | SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis |\\\\n| `references/checks-apigateway.md` | REST, HTTP, WebSocket APIs and stages |\\\\n| `references/checks-stepfunctions.md` | state machines and ASL definitions |\\\\n| `references/checks-dynamodb.md` | tables, GSIs, backups, capacity |\\\\n| `references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md` | alarm coverage and recommended alarm settings |\\\\n| `references/api-quirks.md` | API responses whose obvious reading is wrong |\\\\n| `references/collection-reference.md` | the API calls and fields to collect per resource family |\\\\n| `references/metrics-and-logs.md` | the metric set per resource type and the log pattern table |\\\\n| `references/lambda-runtime-deprecations.md` | runtime end-of-support dates |\\\\n| `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` | finding table, delegation prompt, three result states, outage reply |\\\\n\\\\nEach catalog row carries a check id, pillar, severity, detection rule, remediation, and its AWS\\\\ndocumentation citation. Use the catalog severity as-is.\\\\n\\\\n**Quote the check id in every finding you report**, wherever that finding appears \\\\u2014 the report\\\\nartifact, a chat reply, a one-line summary. \\\\\"SLS-SQS-002\\\\\" lets the reader look up the detection rule\\\\nand its AWS source, and lets two runs be compared line by line; a finding without it is not traceable\\\\nand is not acceptable output. Adjust the catalog severity only for stated context and say so in the\\\\nfinding \\\\u2014 a public function URL the user has confirmed is a public webhook drops from CRITICAL to HIGH.\\\\n\\\\nGroup findings by Well-Architected pillar for the report: Security, Reliability, Performance\\\\nEfficiency, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 10: Generate Report\\\\n\\\\nUse the structure in `references/report-template.md`.\\\\n\\\\n**Artifact naming and granularity:**\\\\n\\\\n- Targeted review of one to three named resources \\\\u2014 one artifact per resource, named\\\\n  `serverless-review-<resource-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`\\\\n- Anything wider (stack, tag, Region, account) \\\\u2014 a single consolidated artifact named\\\\n  `serverless-review-<scope-label>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` with a per-resource section inside\\\\n\\\\nSection order, which matches the other operation-review skills in this repository:\\\\n\\\\n1. Report Header\\\\n2. Executive Summary \\\\u2014 health verdict, finding counts by severity, top 3 critical/high items\\\\n3. Scope Covered \\\\u2014 Regions reviewed, Regions skipped as empty, resources truncated by budget, checks\\\\n   skipped for missing permissions\\\\n4. Configuration Snapshot\\\\n5. Findings by Pillar \\\\u2014 Security, Reliability, Performance, Cost, Operational Excellence\\\\n6. CloudWatch Metrics (7-Day)\\\\n7. Log Pattern Analysis\\\\n8. Alarm Coverage\\\\n9. Cost Summary\\\\n10. Priority Matrix\\\\n11. Next Steps \\\\u2014 Immediate / Short-term / Long-term, per the severity SLAs\\\\n12. Appendix \\\\u2014 reference links\\\\n\\\\nEvery finding must carry: what was observed (with the concrete value), why it matters, the\\\\nrecommendation, and a remediation snippet (AWS CLI, SAM/CloudFormation, or CDK). Never present a\\\\nfinding without evidence.\\\\n\\\\n### Before you present anything \\\\u2014 check your own output\\\\n\\\\nA review that is confidently wrong is worse than one that admits a gap. Run this list against the\\\\nreport, and equally against the answer you type in chat, and fix what fails before presenting either:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] **Evidence on every finding.** Each one names the observed value, not just the conclusion. If a\\\\n      finding says \\\\\"no DLQ configured\\\\\" without naming the absent fields, add them.\\\\n- [ ] **Severities match the catalogs.** Re-read the check id you assigned. If you adjusted a severity\\\\n      for context, the finding says so and says why.\\\\n- [ ] **No invented thresholds.** Every numeric threshold traces to a catalog row. Where AWS publishes\\\\n      none, the finding says the threshold is workload-specific.\\\\n- [ ] **Absent metrics are not findings.** A metric with no datapoints because the configuration does\\\\n      not emit it was omitted, not reported as a failure.\\\\n- [ ] **Cost figures are marked (estimated)** and the split method is stated. No estimate is presented\\\\n      as a bill.\\\\n- [ ] **No secret values anywhere.** Environment variables appear by key name only. Nothing\\\\n      credential-shaped from a log line was reproduced.\\\\n- [ ] **Scope Covered is complete.** Every Region skipped, resource truncated, and check that could not\\\\n      run is listed \\\\u2014 including the ones denied by permission or platform restriction.\\\\n- [ ] **Counts reconcile.** The severity counts in the Executive Summary equal the findings in the body.\\\\n- [ ] **The verdict follows the rule.** Any CRITICAL means \\\\u274c; otherwise any HIGH means \\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f; otherwise \\\\u2705.\\\\n\\\\nIf a check in this list cannot be satisfied, say so where you present the findings rather than\\\\nquietly dropping it.\\\\n\\\\n### When the answer is a chat reply\\\\n\\\\nThe report often goes to an artifact while the user reads only what you type back. That reply is the\\\\nreview in short form, and every rule above holds in it unchanged: each finding keeps its check id,\\\\nobserved value, severity and recommendation, and each threshold keeps its source. Use the finding\\\\ntable in `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md`. {"id": "000009ca-0000-4000-8000-0000000009ca", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_h6EcWurdxQ3vD3BUxUTRy6", "content": "[{'text': '# Check Catalog \u2014 AWS Lambda\\n\\nEvery row carries a check id, pillar, severity, detection rule, and its AWS source. Use the severity\\nas written. Adjust only for context the user has confirmed, and say so in the finding.\\n\\nPillar codes: **SEC** Security \u00b7 **REL** Reliability \u00b7 **PERF** Performance Efficiency \u00b7\\n**COST** Cost Optimization \u00b7 **OPS** Operational Excellence\\n\\nSources referenced throughout:\\n\\n- [Lens \u2014 Failure management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/failure-management.html)\\n- [Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/opex-metrics-and-alerts.html)\\n- [Lens \u2014 Limits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/limits.html)\\n- [Lambda best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html)\\n- [CloudWatch recommended alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Best_Practice_Recommended_Alarms_AWS_Services.html)\\n- [Lambda security best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-security-best-practices.html)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Reliability \u2014 asynchronous invocation\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-001 | REL | HIGH | Function is invoked asynchronously (has an EventBridge, SNS, S3, or `InvocationType: Event` caller) and has **neither** `DeadLetterConfig.TargetArn` **nor** `EventInvokeConfig.DestinationConfig.OnFailure` | Configure an `OnFailure` destination (SQS queue, SNS topic, EventBridge bus, or another function) | Lens \u2014 Failure management: \"Use a dead-letter queue mechanism to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-002 | REL | CRITICAL | `AsyncEventsDropped` > 0 over the 7-day window | Events are being lost. Add an `OnFailure` destination, then raise `MaximumEventAgeInSeconds` / `MaximumRetryAttempts` or fix the failing invocations | Lens \u2014 Failure management |\\n| SLS-LMB-003 | REL | MEDIUM | `EventInvokeConfig` absent or `MaximumRetryAttempts` left at the default `2` on a function whose failures are not idempotent-safe to replay | Set `MaximumRetryAttempts` deliberately (0 for non-retryable work with a destination, higher for transient-failure workloads) | Lambda async invocation defaults |\\n| SLS-LMB-004 | REL | MEDIUM | `MaximumEventAgeInSeconds` left at the default 21,600 s (6 h) on a latency-sensitive workload | Lower the maximum event age so stale events are discarded to the destination rather than retried hours later | Lambda async invocation defaults |\\n| SLS-LMB-005 | REL | HIGH | `DeadLetterErrors` > 0 | Lambda could not write to the configured DLQ \u2014 usually a missing `sqs:SendMessage`/`sns:Publish` permission on the execution role, or a deleted target | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts (alert on `DeadLetterErrors`) |\\n| SLS-LMB-006 | REL | HIGH | `DestinationDeliveryFailures` > 0 | The `OnFailure`/`OnSuccess` destination is unreachable or the execution role lacks permission to write to it | Lambda destinations |\\n| SLS-LMB-007 | REL | LOW | Function uses only the legacy `DeadLetterConfig` and no `OnFailure` destination | Migrate to an `OnFailure` destination: it carries the full invocation record including the response and error, where the DLQ carries only the payload | Lambda destinations |\\n\\n## Reliability \u2014 errors, recursion, and idempotency\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-010 | REL | HIGH | Error rate (`Errors / Invocations`) \u2265 1% over the window | Investigate the top log error patterns from Step 5; add or tune `Retry` at the caller | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Errors`, threshold \"greater than zero\", tolerance-based |\\n| SLS-LMB-011 | REL | CRITICAL | Error rate \u2265 10% over the window | Treat as an active incident, not a review finding | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Errors` |\\n| SLS-LMB-012 | REL | CRITICAL | Log scan matches `Recursive invocation` / `recursive loop detected`, or the function writes to its own trigger | Lambda\\'s recursive loop detection has fired. Break the loop; as immediate containment set reserved concurrency to `0` to throttle all invocations while the code is fixed | Lambda best practices: \"Avoid using recursive invocations\u2026 set the function reserved concurrency to `0` immediately\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-013 | REL | LOW | Function consumes from an event source mapping (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, MSK) \u2014 idempotency cannot be verified from configuration | Confirm the handler is idempotent. Event source mappings process each event **at least once** and duplicates do occur | Lambda best practices: \"Write idempotent code\"; ESM warning on duplicate processing |\\n| SLS-LMB-014 | REL | MEDIUM | `Timeout` is at or near the 900 s maximum on a synchronous, user-facing path | A long timeout converts a downstream hang into held concurrency. Bound the timeout to the real p99 plus headroom and fail fast | Lambda best practices: \"Load test your Lambda function to determine an optimum timeout value\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-015 | REL | MEDIUM | Function is VPC-attached and the log scan matches `EC2ThrottledException` or `ENILimitReached` | Hyperplane ENI capacity or subnet IP exhaustion. Add subnet IP space across more AZs and check the ENI quota | Lambda VPC networking |\\n| SLS-LMB-016 | REL | LOW | Function is VPC-attached with subnets in fewer than two Availability Zones | A single-AZ subnet set makes the function fail with the AZ | Lens \u2014 Reliability foundations |\\n\\n## Reliability and scaling \u2014 concurrency\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-020 | REL | HIGH | `ClaimedAccountConcurrency` \u2265 90% of `AccountLimit.ConcurrentExecutions` | Request a concurrency quota increase, release unused reserved or provisioned concurrency, improve function throughput, or raise event source batch sizes | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `ClaimedAccountConcurrency`, \"about 90% of the concurrency quota set for the account in the Region\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-021 | REL | MEDIUM | `ClaimedAccountConcurrency` between 70% and 90% of the quota | Plan headroom before the next traffic increase; the default Region quota is 1,000 | CloudWatch recommended alarms; Lens \u2014 Limits |\\n| SLS-LMB-022 | REL | HIGH | `Throttles` > 0 on a synchronous, user-facing function | Requests are being rejected. Add reserved concurrency to protect this function, use provisioned concurrency for latency-critical paths, and add timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter at the caller | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Throttles`; Lambda best practices \"Build in throttle tolerance\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-023 | REL | MEDIUM | `Throttles` > 0 on an async or stream-driven function | Throttled async invocations are retried, but retries consume event age. Confirm the retry budget and destination are set | Lambda best practices |\\n| SLS-LMB-024 | REL | MEDIUM | A business-critical function has no `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` while other functions in the account are unreserved and high-volume | Without reserved concurrency, a noisy neighbour can consume the shared pool and starve this function | Lambda best practices: \"If you need to limit how high your function can scale, you can configure reserved concurrency\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-025 | REL | CRITICAL | `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` is `0` and the function is not intentionally disabled | Reserved concurrency of zero throttles the function completely. Confirm whether this is deliberate containment or an accident | Lambda concurrency |\\n| SLS-LMB-026 | REL | HIGH | Function calls a downstream with a fixed connection ceiling (RDS, self-managed database, third-party API) and has no reserved concurrency | Lambda scales faster than most downstreams. Cap it with reserved concurrency and pool connections (RDS Proxy for relational targets) | Lambda best practices: \"Be familiar with your upstream and downstream throughput constraints\" |\\n\\n## Performance efficiency\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-030 | PERF | HIGH | `Duration` p99 \u2265 90% of the configured `Timeout` | The function is on the edge of timing out. Either raise the timeout with evidence or reduce the work per invocation | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Duration`: \"Make sure to set the threshold lower than the configured function timeout\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-031 | PERF | MEDIUM | `Duration` p99 between 70% and 90% of `Timeout` | Little headroom for a slow downstream day | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Duration` |\\n| SLS-LMB-032 | PERF | HIGH | REPORT line carries `Status: timeout`, or the log scan matches `Task timed out`, or `Duration` equals the configured `Timeout` almost exactly | Invocations are being killed at the timeout. Correlate with downstream latency before raising the timeout. Current managed runtimes record this as `Status: timeout` on the REPORT line and may emit no `Task timed out` message \u2014 scan for both | Lambda best practices; verified against a live test bed |\\n| SLS-LMB-033 | PERF | HIGH | Peak `Max Memory Used` \u2265 90% of `MemorySize`, **or** the log scan matches `Runtime.OutOfMemory` / `Runtime exited` (runtime killed) **or** a language-level allocator failure \u2014 `MemoryError` (Python), `JavaScript heap out of memory` (Node.js), `OutOfMemoryError` (Java) | Raise `MemorySize`; note this also raises CPU proportionally | Lambda best practices: analyse `Max Memory Used`; CloudWatch recommends alarming Lambda Insights `memory_utilization` at 90% |\\n| SLS-LMB-033a | PERF | HIGH | A language-level allocator failure appears in the logs while `Max Memory Used` reports a low figure | Do not dismiss the finding because the metric looks healthy. When the allocator refuses a large allocation up front the pages are never touched, so `Max Memory Used` under-reports. Observed in practice: a 128 MB function failing with `MemoryError` reported `Max Memory Used: 35 MB` | verified against a live test bed |\\n| SLS-LMB-034 | PERF | MEDIUM | Function is behind an API Gateway REST/HTTP integration and `Timeout` > 29 s | API Gateway\\'s integration timeout caps the request well before the function\\'s own timeout, so the client sees a 504 while the function keeps running and billing | API Gateway quotas |\\n| SLS-LMB-035 | PERF | MEDIUM | Cold starts exceed 5% of invocations on a synchronous, latency-sensitive path, or p99 `Init Duration` > 1 s | Move SDK client and connection setup outside the handler, trim the deployment package, consider SnapStart (Java) or provisioned concurrency | Lambda best practices: \"Take advantage of execution environment reuse\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-036 | PERF | MEDIUM | `ProvisionedConcurrencySpilloverInvocations` > 0 | Traffic is exceeding the provisioned pool and falling back to on-demand cold starts. Raise provisioned concurrency or add autoscaling on the alias | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts: \"When provisioned concurrency is enabled, use `ProvisionedConcurrencySpilloverInvocations`\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-037 | PERF | LOW | `PostRuntimeExtensionsDuration` is a material share of `Duration` | An extension or layer is adding billed time after the handler returns. Audit the extensions in use | Lambda extensions |\\n| SLS-LMB-038 | PERF | LOW | Java function with no `SnapStart` and a high `Init Duration` | SnapStart materially reduces Java cold start | Lambda SnapStart |\\n| SLS-LMB-039 | PERF | LOW | Log scan shows repeated `connect ETIMEDOUT` / `SocketTimeout` on a function that reuses connections | Apply the runtime\\'s keep-alive directive; Lambda purges idle connections and reusing a dead one errors | Lambda best practices: \"Use a keep-alive directive to maintain persistent connections\" |\\n\\n## Security\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-050 | SEC | CRITICAL | `Runtime` deprecation date is in the past | Upgrade to a supported runtime \u2014 see `lambda-runtime-deprecations.md` | Lambda runtime deprecation policy |\\n| SLS-LMB-051 | SEC | HIGH | `Runtime` deprecation date within 180 days, or the runtime is AL2-based (AL2 reached end of life 2026-06-30), or the runtime is a public preview runtime | Plan the upgrade now; preview runtimes must not carry production workloads | Lambda runtimes page |\\n| SLS-LMB-052 | SEC | CRITICAL | Execution role grants `AdministratorAccess`, or any statement with `\"Action\": \"*\"` and `\"Resource\": \"*\"` | Replace with least-privilege actions scoped to the specific resource ARNs the handler touches | Lambda best practices: \"Use most-restrictive permissions when setting IAM policies\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-053 | SEC | HIGH | Execution role grants a service-level wildcard (`s3:*`, `dynamodb:*`, `sqs:*`) or `iam:PassRole` on `Resource: \"*\"` | Enumerate the actions actually used and scope resources | Lambda best practices |\\n| SLS-LMB-054 | SEC | HIGH | Role trust policy allows a principal other than `lambda.amazonaws.com` with no condition, or allows a wildcard principal | Restrict the trust policy; add `aws:SourceAccount` / `aws:SourceArn` conditions | IAM best practices |\\n| SLS-LMB-055 | SEC | CRITICAL | Resource-based policy (`lambda:GetPolicy`) contains `\"Principal\": \"*\"` or `{\"AWS\": \"*\"}` with no `SourceArn` or `SourceAccount` condition | Scope the statement to the specific calling service or account | Lambda resource-based policies |\\n| SLS-LMB-056 | SEC | CRITICAL | Function URL with `AuthType: NONE` | This is a public unauthenticated HTTPS endpoint. Switch to `AWS_IAM`, or if it must stay public, front it with CloudFront and AWS WAF and confirm the handler validates every input. Drops to HIGH only when the user confirms the public exposure is intentional | Lambda function URLs |\\n| SLS-LMB-057 | SEC | MEDIUM | Function URL with permissive CORS (`AllowOrigins: [\"*\"]`) on an authenticated endpoint | Restrict allowed origins | Lambda function URL CORS |\\n| SLS-LMB-058 | SEC | MEDIUM | Environment variables present, `KMSKeyArn` absent, and at least one key name matches `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN`, `API_KEY`, `APIKEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `CREDENTIAL`, `CONNECTION_STRING`, `DSN`, `AUTH` | Move the value to AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store and read it at init; if it must stay an environment variable, encrypt with a customer-managed KMS key. **Report the key name only \u2014 never the value** | Lambda security best practices; Lambda environment variable encryption |\\n| SLS-LMB-059 | SEC | LOW | Environment variables present with no `KMSKeyArn` and no secret-suggesting key names | Environment variables are encrypted at rest with an AWS-managed key by default; a customer-managed key adds auditability and key-policy control | Lambda environment variables |\\n| SLS-LMB-060 | SEC | LOW | No `CodeSigningConfigArn` | Code signing verifies the deployment package was produced by a trusted publisher | Lambda code signing |\\n| SLS-LMB-061 | SEC | HIGH | Log scan surfaces what appears to be a credential, token, or connection string in a log line | Report the log group and the pattern that matched \u2014 **never the value**. Redact at the source and rotate the exposed credential | Lambda best practices; Lens \u2014 logging |\\n| SLS-LMB-062 | SEC | MEDIUM | Function is VPC-attached with a security group allowing unrestricted egress `0.0.0.0/0` on all ports, where the workload only needs specific destinations | Scope egress rules to required destinations and use VPC endpoints for AWS services | Security best practices |\\n| SLS-LMB-063 | SEC | INFO | Account has neither GuardDuty Lambda Protection nor Security Hub Lambda controls enabled | Both give continuous detection that a point-in-time review cannot | Lambda best practices \u2014 security best practices section |\\n\\n## Cost optimization\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-070 | COST | MEDIUM | Peak `Max Memory Used` < 60% of `MemorySize` | Over-provisioned memory. Validate with AWS Lambda Power Tuning before changing \u2014 lowering memory also lowers CPU and can raise duration and total cost | Lambda best practices: \"By analyzing the `Max Memory Used:` field, you can determine if your function needs more memory or if you over-provisioned\"; Lambda Power Tuning |\\n| SLS-LMB-071 | COST | MEDIUM | `Architectures: [\"x86_64\"]` on a supported runtime | All supported runtimes support `arm64`. Graviton gives better price/performance. Rebuild container images, native binaries, and architecture-specific layers first, then cut over with a weighted alias | Lambda runtimes: \"All supported Lambda runtimes support both x86_64 and arm64 architectures\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-072 | COST | MEDIUM | Log group `retentionInDays` is absent (never expire) | Set a retention period matched to the operational and compliance need \u2014 30 days for most application logs, longer only where required | CloudWatch Logs retention |\\n| SLS-LMB-073 | COST | LOW | Log group `storedBytes` is large relative to invocation count | Reduce log verbosity, use `ApplicationLogLevel` to filter at source, and prefer EMF over verbose logging for metrics. Ingestion is typically the larger cost line than storage | Lambda advanced logging controls; Lambda best practices \u2014 EMF |\\n| SLS-LMB-074 | COST | MEDIUM | Provisioned concurrency configured with persistently low `ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization` and no `ProvisionedConcurrencySpilloverInvocations` | The pool is paid for and idle. Reduce it, or replace with scheduled autoscaling that matches the traffic curve | Lambda provisioned concurrency: \"Configuring provisioned concurrency incurs additional charges\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-075 | COST | LOW | Zero `Invocations` over the window and `LastModified` older than 90 days | Delete unused functions \u2014 they count against the deployment package storage quota | Lambda best practices: \"Delete Lambda functions that you are no longer using\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-076 | COST | LOW | Very short `Duration` (single-digit ms) with a large `BatchSize` of 1 on a queue or stream source | Larger batches amortise invocation overhead across more records and raise throughput | Lambda best practices: \"Test with different batch and record sizes\" |\\n| SLS-LMB-077 | COST | INFO | Account has no AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor covering Lambda | Cost Anomaly Detection catches runaway invocation cost that a periodic review will miss | Lambda best practices: \"Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection\" |\\n\\n## Operational excellence\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-LMB-080 | OPS | MEDIUM | No CloudWatch alarm on `Errors` | See `cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md` for the recommended alarm definition | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts |\\n| SLS-LMB-081 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `Throttles` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts |\\n| SLS-LMB-082 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `Duration` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts |\\n| SLS-LMB-083 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `ConcurrentExecutions` or `ClaimedAccountConcurrency` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts |\\n| SLS-LMB-084 | OPS | MEDIUM | Stream-driven function with no alarm on `IteratorAge` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts; Lambda best practices recommends a 30,000 ms `IteratorAge` alarm |\\n| SLS-LMB-085 | OPS | MEDIUM | Async function with no alarm on `DeadLetterErrors` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts |\\n| SLS-LMB-086 | OPS | MEDIUM | `TracingConfig.Mode` is `PassThrough` | Enable Active tracing for distributed tracing across the invocation path | Lens \u2014 Distributed tracing |\\n| SLS-LMB-087 | OPS | LOW | `LoggingConfig.LogFormat` is `Text` | Structured JSON logging makes logs searchable and filterable; **Checked and clean:**
- **Resource policies:** all are scoped by `SourceArn`. There is no `Principal: *` (SLS-LMB-055).
- **Function URLs:** only one exists, and it is not public (SLS-LMB-056).
- **Role trust:** the one role I read trusts only `lambda.amazonaws.com`.
- **Throttles:** measured 0 on all 8 invoked functions.
- **Duration p99 vs timeout:** every function has more than 10× headroom.
- **Account concurrency:** 1.6% of quota.

### Context (not counted, no check id or outside the window)
- **`exb-dispatcher` is failing quietly.**
  - It logged 120,984 `ERROR` lines in 7 days. All say `reconcile-failed … Requested resource not found`.
  - Its `Errors` metric is 0 across 10,087 invocations, so the function handles the failure internally.
  - Its three alarms (errors, throttles, DLQ-not-empty) have no alarm actions, so they would not notify anyone even if they fired.
  - My guess is a missing DynamoDB table or similar resource, but I haven't confirmed it.
- **`ExampleCleanupLambda`:** 185 `ERROR` lines and 5 `AccessDenied` lines, last at 15:31Z today.
- **Stale test-bed evidence:** `slsreview-always-times-out` and `slsreview-memory-hog` have 0 invocations in the window. Their older logs, from Sep 10 to Oct 17, show `Status: timeout` at 5000 ms. They also show a `MemoryError` at 128 MB while reporting 35 MB used. Those would map to SLS-LMB-032 and SLS-LMB-033a if they recurred. I did not count them.
- **Cost:** Lambda spend was about $0.0036 per month for Aug–Oct (Cost Explorer). The memory, Graviton, and retention findings are real but save almost nothing. Memory changes should go through Lambda Power Tuning.

## Could not check
- **Never queried:**
  - Reserved concurrency and tags for 24 of 30 functions.
  - Async invoke config for 22 of 30 (the 8 I checked all returned defaults).
  - Aliases, versions, and provisioned concurrency.
  - Function `State` and `LastUpdateStatus`.
  - GuardDuty Lambda Protection and Cost Anomaly Detection.
  - SQS and DLQ depth metrics.
  - EventBridge rule targets (SLS-EVB-001 and similar), even though 6 functions are rule-triggered.
- **IAM coverage is partial.**
  - `iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails` was denied.
  - Of 20 distinct execution roles, I read attached policy names for 13 and inline policy names for 2. I read a full policy document for only 1.
  - `EXBLambdaCompletionHandlerRole` has `AWSTransformCustomFullAccess`. That is a possible SLS-LMB-053 hit, but I didn't open the policy.
  - 7 roles were not examined at all.
- **No datapoints:** 22 functions had no invocations in the window, so there is no runtime evidence for them either way. Their `Errors` metric emitted nothing, which is not a pass.

## Confidence
- **High (config-derived):** the runtime, SQS timing, stream mapping, function URL, resource-policy, and `slsreview` role findings are direct API reads. The metric counts for `slsreview-legacy-runtime` match its logs, and its 6 invocations show in both.
- **Medium (7-day behavior):**
  - Only 8 of 30 functions had traffic, and the `slsreview-*` functions were created at 17:46Z today.
  - My first log reads returned empty or partial pages. I caught that by cross-checking against metrics and redid it with Logs Insights (22 log groups, 175,724 records).
  - Runtime dates come from a reference table last verified 2026-09-10. I confirmed python3.9 against current docs. Its block-create dates differ from the live page, so the table is partly stale. I did not confirm python3.11's date, which doesn't change the AL2-based HIGH.
- **Low:** any claim of "healthy" for the 22 idle functions, for IAM least-privilege on most roles, and for EventBridge reliability.
- **How to read the criticals.**
  - The slsreview functions, the `serverless-review-testbed` stack role, and the error text "deliberate … failure" all point to a deliberately flawed test bed. Treat SLS-LMB-050, 011, 002, STR-001, and most HIGHs as expected.
  - The risks that matter on real workloads are:
    - the quiet `exb-dispatcher` failures
    - the missing DLQs on EventBridge-triggered functions
    - python3.11 on AL2
    - the alarm gaps

## Recommendations
This review is read-only, so none of these were applied.

1. **Investigate `exb-dispatcher`'s `reconcile-failed` errors.** Add an alarm action to its existing alarms, and an alarm on a metric filter for the `ERROR` log pattern.
2. **Add an `OnFailure` destination to the 6 EventBridge-invoked functions (SLS-LMB-001).**
   ```bash
   aws lambda put-function-event-invoke-config --function-name <fn> \
     --maximum-retry-attempts 2 --maximum-event-age-in-seconds 3600 \
     --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:<acct>:<failure-queue>"}}'
   ```
3. **Plan the `example-agent-*` move from python3.11 to python3.13.** Test on a version and alias first. Fix `slsreview-legacy-runtime` the same way if it is meant to live.
4. **Harden the stream and SQS consumers (STR-001 to 006, SQS-002/003/006).**
   ```bash
   aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid <stream-uuid> --maximum-retry-attempts 5 \
     --maximum-record-age-in-seconds 3600 --bisect-batch-on-function-error \
     --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures \
     --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"<sqs-arn>"}}'
   aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url <url> --attributes VisibilityTimeout=360
   ```
   Also attach a DLQ with `maxReceiveCount` of at least 5, and enable partial batch responses on the SQS mapping.
5. **Scope `far-too-broad` to the specific table, queue, and topic ARNs (SLS-LMB-053).**
6. **Add the core alarms with `--alarm-actions`.**
   - `Errors` Sum >0, 60 s, 3/3.
   - `Throttles` Sum ≥ threshold, 60 s, 5/5.
   - `Duration` p90 below each function's timeout, 15/15.
   - `ClaimedAccountConcurrency` Max about 900 (90% of 1,000), 10/10.
   - `IteratorAge` Max >30,000 ms, 15/15 (the Lambda best practices example).
   - `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` on the queue.
7. **Lower-priority housekeeping:** set 30-day log retention, enable JSON logging and active tracing, and tag for ownership. Try arm64 only for the larger or busier functions.

If you want me to finish the unchecked parts, I'd start with the IAM role documents and the EventBridge rule targets.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
